flagged.evidence: The proof says, “Coupling any two chains with these same updates makes them coincide by that block with probability at least δ>0, and after coincidence they stay equal. After k blocks their disagreement probability is at most (1−δ)^k.” For the two different parameters just introduced, this is false: on a one-edge graph with q=1, p₁=1/4 and p₂=3/4, after both chains are closed, a shared update uniform U=1/2 leaves the p₁ chain closed and opens the p₂ chain. Equality is not absorbing across different transition kernels, so the stated block bound does not justify convergence of this coupled pair; separate same-kernel convergence arguments are needed before taking the order limit.
